interpretation: The development run is consistent with direct attack on the rooted reproductive pool preceding a delayed fielded-force response.
Two of eight worlds rebound above baseline rooted membership by day 360, indicating substantial state dependence rather than deterministic durable suppression.

The security-surge interaction is contaminated by target-normalization semantics: raising police/military targets lowers the normalized local-security score before staffing catches up, reducing intelligence penetration and underground-disruption efficiency. It is treated as a model-design diagnostic, not a substantive COIN finding.
Administrative-surge effects were negligible at the tested intensity because cumulative rebuild was tiny relative to existing administrative stocks.
